div.l: Now by my fadres soule / that is ded
But ȝe be merye / I wol ȝeue ȝow myn hed
Holdeth vp ȝoure hondes / withoute more speche
Oure counseill / was nought longe for to seche
Vs thoughte it was not worth / to make it wys
And graunted hym / withoute more avys
And bad hym say / his verdite as hym leste
Lordinges qd he / now herkeneth for the beste
But take it nought / I pray ȝow in disdeyn
This is the poynt / to speke short and pleyn
That ech of ȝow to shorte with oure weye
In this viage / shal telle tales tweye
To Caunt̉erbury ward I mene it so
And homward he shall tellen other two
Of auentures / that whilom haue befalle
And which of ȝow / that bereth hym best of alle
That is to seyn / that telleth in this caas
Tales of best sentence / and of moost solas
Shal haue a soper / at oure alther cost
Here in this place / sittinge by this post
Whan that we comen a geyn / fro Cauntirbury
And for to make ȝow / the more mery
I wol my self / goodly with ȝow ryde
Right at myn owne cost and be ȝoure gyde
And who so wole / my iugement withseye
Shall paie for al / we spende by the weye
And ȝif ȝe vouchesauf / that it be so
Tel me anon / withoute wordes mo
And I wol erly / shape me therfore
This thing was graunted / and oure othes swore
With ful glad herte and prayen hym also
That he wolde vouchesauf for to done so
And he wolde ben oure goủernour
And of oure tales / Iuge and reportour
And sette a soper / at a certeyn prys
And we wol rewled ben / at his deuys
In high and low / and thus by oon assent
We ben accorded / to the iugement
And ther vpon / the wyn was fet anon
